subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` gain user-controlled exclude patterns now, and should the permanent shape follow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower explicit-excludes-only design?
rationale: The feature adds public CLI surface and backup selection policy that affects both sensitive-data exposure and restore completeness, so automation cannot safely choose the default/protected-path semantics.

options.title: Review the linked native PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the product/security review vehicle, requiring real backup proof and explicit decisions on defaults, implicit ignore files, and protected paths before merge.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes
options.body: Ask for a smaller implementation with repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` only, deferring smart defaults and auto-detected ignore files.

options.title: Defer native controls
options.body: Keep native backup coarse for now and direct users to external backup tooling while maintainers decide whether core should own exclusion policy.

recommendation.title: Review the linked native PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the product/security review vehicle, requiring real backup proof and explicit decisions on defaults, implicit ignore files, and protected paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The original backup CLI history makes shichangs the best available owner for native backup command semantics.
